title: HIS-201 Ch. 5 — 3 Numbers & Dates
subject: HIS-201
topic: Chapter 5: The Mosaic of Eighteenth-Century America

cards.def: In 1690 Spain began establishing missions among Texas Indians as a buffer against the French.

cards.term: When Spain first explored and then colonized California
cards.def: Spaniards first explored California's coast in 1542, but the Crown authorized permanent colonization only in 1768.

cards.term: How many French lived along the St. Lawrence by 1760
cards.def: By 1760 about 75,000 French colonists, soldiers and priests lived in the St. Lawrence valley, mostly through natural increase.
In 1698 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville founded French Louisiana with a post at Biloxi Bay.

cards.term: When the Company of the Indies brought slaves to Louisiana
cards.def: In 1719 the Company of the Indies brought nearly 6,000 slaves, overwhelmingly men, directly from Africa to Louisiana.

cards.term: When the Natchez rose against the French
cards.def: In 1729 the Natchez, joined by some newly arrived slaves, rose against the French and killed or captured about 500 colonists.

cards.term: When King William's War and Queen Anne's War were fought
cards.def: King William's War was fought from 1689 to 1697 and Queen Anne's War from 1702 to 1713, followed by about 25 years of Anglo-French "cold war" over trade.

cards.term: How many British and French colonists there were in 1720
cards.def: In 1720 Britain had nearly 400,000 colonial subjects and France only about 25,000, yet France's Indian alliances blocked British expansion west of the Appalachians.

cards.term: How many Scots-Irish, Germans and Africans came in the 1700s
cards.def: In the 1700s about 250,000 Africans in chains, about 250,000 Scots-Irish and about 135,000 Germans came to the British colonies.

cards.term: How high the colonial birthrate was
cards.def: The colonial birthrate was triple today's, with most women bearing five to eight children and most children surviving to adulthood.

cards.term: How many Americans were of African ancestry in 1775
cards.def: By 1775 one in five Americans was of African ancestry, and over 90 percent of black Americans lived in the South.

cards.term: When slave imports to the South peaked
cards.def: The four decades after 1700 were the heaviest years of slave importation to the Chesapeake and Carolina.
In 1739 nearly 100 Africans led by Jemmy rose in South Carolina's Stono Rebellion, the largest slave revolt of the colonial period.
The Great Awakening first appeared in the 1730s among Presbyterians and Congregationalists in the middle colonies and New England.
George Whitefield arrived in fall 1739 and preached from Georgia to New Hampshire for two years, sailing home in 1741.

cards.term: When Presbyterian and Baptist churches spread south
cards.def: From the mid-1740s to the 1770s scores of new Presbyterian and Baptist churches formed in the South and backcountry.

cards.term: How big the middle class was in England and America
cards.def: Less than one-third of the English were middle class, compared with nearly three-quarters of white colonists.
